checkClasses.name: structure
checkClasses.detail: Every element of every resource is resolved against the R4 4.0.1 definition of its type; an element R4 does not define, a resource with no type, and an ambiguous choice element are errors.

checkClasses.name: element cardinality
checkClasses.detail: Minimum and maximum cardinality of every direct element, from the R4 4.0.1 snapshot, plus any cardinality the applied profile tightens.

checkClasses.name: primitive value domain
checkClasses.detail: The lexical form of every primitive is checked against its R4 datatype pattern.

checkClasses.name: required-binding membership
checkClasses.detail: Enforced for every `code` element whose required-strength value set expands offline from the pinned packages alone. A binding needing a filter, an exclusion, or a code system the packages do not publish complete is NOT evaluated; the counts are published beside this list.

checkClasses.name: profile fixed and pattern values
checkClasses.detail: `fixed[x]` and `pattern[x]` constraints of every applied profile.

checkClasses.name: profile slicing
checkClasses.detail: Slice membership by `value`, `pattern` and `exists` discriminators. A slicing whose discriminator cannot be evaluated is reported unchecked rather than passed.

checkClasses.name: must-support
checkClasses.detail: Reported at information severity only, never as an error: must-support is a system obligation, not an instance-presence requirement, so it never affects the passing count.

checkClasses.name: FHIRPath invariants
checkClasses.detail: Constraints on the base R4 definition and on every applied profile are evaluated where the expression is within the engine's FHIRPath subset; anything outside it is reported unchecked, at information severity, and never counted as a pass.

checkClasses.name: external terminology resolution
checkClasses.detail: No terminology server is consulted and none is bundled. Membership in a value set drawn from SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, UCUM or any other externally-maintained system is NOT checked.

checkClasses.name: reference resolution across the Bundle
checkClasses.detail: Whether a `Reference` resolves to an entry of the same Bundle is not evaluated here; the library's own property suite covers dangling `urn:uuid:` references.

checkClasses.name: mapping correctness
checkClasses.detail: Nothing here says the right v2 field reached the right FHIR element. A zero-error result says the FHIR is well formed and conforms to the profiles named, not that the transform is right.

profileScope.reason: The one AllergyIntolerance profile the package publishes.
US Core 9.0.0 publishes no Appointment profile. Validated against base R4 4.0.1 alone, and never recorded as profile-conformant.
US Core 9.0.0 publishes no Bundle profile. Validated against base R4 4.0.1 alone, and never recorded as profile-conformant.
The one Coverage profile the package publishes.

The package publishes two DiagnosticReport profiles, one for laboratory results and one for clinical notes. The corpus carries one DiagnosticReport, from the ORU_R01, whose OBR-4 is a LOINC laboratory order and whose OBX results are laboratory values, so the laboratory profile is the one that applies.

The package publishes two DocumentReference profiles, the general one and one scoped to advance-directive documents. The corpus carries one DocumentReference, from the MDM_T02, whose TXA-2 document type is a discharge summary and not an advance directive, so the general profile is the one that applies.
The one Encounter profile the package publishes.
The one Immunization profile the package publishes.
US Core 9.0.0 publishes no MessageHeader profile. Validated against base R4 4.0.1 alone, and never recorded as profile-conformant.

Every Observation profile the package publishes is topic-scoped, so no resource can satisfy them all and applying them all would measure conformance to a set nothing can conform to. How many it publishes is printed beside this reason, read off the package itself rather than written here. The default applied is the package's own catch-all for observations no other profile covers.

perMessage.reason: The ORU_R01's three Observations are laboratory results, each carrying a LOINC code and a quantity, so the laboratory-result profile applies to them rather than the catch-all.
